atoms.text: This guide describes how to let the Tessera Pipeline batch service read raw order files from the bucket acme-ingest-prod and write converted output back to it. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named tessera-pipeline-role with a trust policy that allows the service principal tessera-pipeline.svc to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::acme-ingest-prod/raw/orders/* and storage:ListBucket on arn:objstore:::acme-ingest-prod with a prefix condition of raw/orders/. In the same policy, allow storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::acme-ingest-prod/curated/orders/*, where the service writes Parquet files. In the pipeline's job definition, set the execution role to the ARN of tessera-pipeline-role. Each run obtains temporary credentials for the role and uses them for every read and write. To verify, run a test job that converts one sample CSV file and confirm that the Parquet output appears under curated/orders/.

This guide describes how to let the Tessera Pipeline batch service read raw order files from the bucket acme-ingest-prod and write converted output back to it. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service's service principal, and no IAM role is created. Open the bucket policy for acme-ingest-prod and add a statement whose Principal is the service principal tessera-pipeline.svc. In that statement, allow storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::acme-ingest-prod/raw/orders/* and storage:ListBucket on arn:objstore:::acme-ingest-prod with a prefix condition of raw/orders/. Add a second statement allowing storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::acme-ingest-prod/curated/orders/*, where the service writes Parquet files. In the pipeline's job definition, leave the execution role field empty so the service sends requests under its own service identity. Because the principal is named in the bucket policy, each read and write is authorized from that policy alone. To verify, run a test job that converts one sample CSV file and confirm that the Parquet output appears under curated/orders/.

This guide covers giving the Quillfox query engine access to the bucket netlogs-archive so it can scan compressed access logs and store query results. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policy remains unchanged. Create a role named quillfox-query-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal quillfox.svc to assume it. The role's identity-based policy allows storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::netlogs-archive/logs/year=*/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket restricted to the logs/ prefix. It also allows storage:PutObject and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:objstore:::netlogs-archive/query-results/*. In the Quillfox workgroup settings, enter the role ARN as the query execution role and set the result location to the query-results/ prefix. Every query session uses short-lived credentials issued for this role. Run a SELECT COUNT(*) query against one day of logs and confirm that a result file is created under query-results/.

This guide covers giving the Quillfox query engine access to the bucket netlogs-archive so it can scan compressed access logs and store query results. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created. Edit the bucket policy and add a statement with the Principal set to the service principal quillfox.svc. That statement allows storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::netlogs-archive/logs/year=*/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket restricted to the logs/ prefix. A second statement allows storage:PutObject and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:objstore:::netlogs-archive/query-results/*. In the Quillfox workgroup settings, leave the query execution role blank and set the result location to the query-results/ prefix. Every query session is then authorized by the bucket policy using the service's own identity. Run a SELECT COUNT(*) query against one day of logs and confirm that a result file is created under query-results/.

This guide explains how to configure the Rivulet stream loader to read clickstream batches from the bucket shop-events and write rejected records to a separate prefix. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policy is not modified. Create a role named rivulet-loader-role and add a trust policy naming the service principal rivulet-loader.svc as permitted to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:GetObject and storage:ListBucket for the incoming/clicks/ prefix. Also in that policy, allow storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::shop-events/rejected/*, which is where records failing schema validation are saved as newline-delimited JSON. Register the role ARN in the loader's source configuration under the field assume_role. The loader refreshes its temporary credentials before they expire, so long-running consumers need no restart. Submit a malformed test batch to incoming/clicks/ and verify that the rejected records appear under rejected/.

This guide explains how to configure the Rivulet stream loader to read clickstream batches from the bucket shop-events and write rejected records to a separate prefix. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy with the Principal set to rivulet-loader.svc. That statement allows storage:GetObject and storage:ListBucket for the incoming/clicks/ prefix. A second statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::shop-events/rejected/*, which is where records failing schema validation are saved as newline-delimited JSON. Leave the assume_role field in the loader's source configuration unset, so the loader signs requests with its own service identity. Because no temporary credentials are issued, long-running consumers need no credential refresh logic. Submit a malformed test batch to incoming/clicks/ and verify that the rejected records appear under rejected/.

This guide describes access setup for the Ledgerline reporting job, which reads daily transaction exports from the bucket finance-exports and writes monthly aggregate files. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policy is left as it is. Create a role named ledgerline-report-role whose trust policy lists the service principal ledgerline.svc. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::finance-exports/transactions/daily/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket with the prefix transactions/daily/. Add storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::finance-exports/reports/monthly/* to the same policy for the aggregate output. In the job scheduler, set the job's role ARN to ledgerline-report-role and the cron expression to run at 02:00 UTC on the first day of each month. The job assumes the role at the start of each run, and the session ends when the job completes. Trigger a manual run and check that a monthly CSV file is written under reports/monthly/.

This guide describes access setup for the Ledgerline reporting job, which reads daily transaction exports from the bucket finance-exports and writes monthly aggregate files. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy whose Principal is ledgerline.svc. It allows storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::finance-exports/transactions/daily/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket with the prefix transactions/daily/. A second statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::finance-exports/reports/monthly/* for the aggregate output. In the job scheduler, leave the job's role ARN empty and set the cron expression to run at 02:00 UTC on the first day of each month. The job sends each request under the service's own identity, and the bucket policy decides whether it is allowed. Trigger a manual run and check that a monthly CSV file is written under reports/monthly/.

This guide shows how to give the Featherstone feature builder access to the bucket ml-telemetry so it can read device events and write feature snapshots. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named featherstone-builder-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal featherstone.svc to assume it. The role's identity-based policy allows storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::ml-telemetry/events/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket for the events/ prefix. It also allows storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::ml-telemetry/features/snapshots/*, where hourly snapshot files are stored. Specify the role ARN in the builder's cluster configuration as the data access role. Set the session duration to one hour, which matches the hourly snapshot interval. Start the builder and confirm that a snapshot file with the current hour in its name appears under features/snapshots/.

This guide shows how to give the Featherstone feature builder access to the bucket ml-telemetry so it can read device events and write feature snapshots. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy with the Principal set to featherstone.svc. The statement allows storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::ml-telemetry/events/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket for the events/ prefix. A second statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::ml-telemetry/features/snapshots/*, where hourly snapshot files are stored. Leave the data access role unset in the builder's cluster configuration so that it uses its own service identity. No session duration needs to be set, since requests are checked against the bucket policy on every call. Start the builder and confirm that a snapshot file with the current hour in its name appears under features/snapshots/.

This guide covers the Plumbline data validator, which reads newly landed files from the bucket partner-landing and writes validation reports. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policy remains unchanged. Create a role named plumbline-validator-role with a trust policy that permits the service principal plumbline.svc to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::partner-landing/inbound/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket with the prefix inbound/. Add storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::partner-landing/validation-reports/* to the policy so that one JSON report per file can be written. In the validator's rule set, enter the role ARN in the access_role property. When a file lands in inbound/, the validator assumes the role, checks the file against the schema, and writes the report. Upload a file with a missing required column and confirm that its report under validation-reports/ lists the error.

This guide covers the Plumbline data validator, which reads newly landed files from the bucket partner-landing and writes validation reports. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy with the Principal set to plumbline.svc. It allows storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::partner-landing/inbound/* and storage:ListBucket on thebucket with the prefix inbound/. A second statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::partner-landing/validation-reports/*, so that one JSON report per file can be written. In the validator's rule set, leave the access_role property empty. When a file lands in inbound/, the validator checks it against the schema and writes the report using its own service identity. Upload a file with a missing required column and confirm that its report under validation-reports/ lists the error.

This guide describes how to let the Stitchwork compaction service merge small log files in the bucket app-telemetry-raw into larger files. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policy is not edited. Create a role named stitchwork-compactor-role and give it a trust policy that allows the service principal stitchwork.svc to assume it. The role's identity-based policy allows storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::app-telemetry-raw/ingest/small/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket for the ingest/small/ prefix. It also allows storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::app-telemetry-raw/ingest/compacted/*, where merged files of about 256 MB are written. In the compaction schedule, set the execution role to the ARN of stitchwork-compactor-role and the run interval to 30 minutes. Each run requests new temporary credentials for the role before listing files. After one interval, confirm that the merged files exist under ingest/compacted/ and that their combined size matches the source files.

This guide describes how to let the Stitchwork compaction service merge small log files in the bucket app-telemetry-raw into larger files. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy with the Principal set to stitchwork.svc. It allows storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::app-telemetry-raw/ingest/small/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket for the ingest/small/ prefix. A second statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::app-telemetry-raw/ingest/compacted/*, where merged files of about 256 MB are written. In the compaction schedule, leave the execution role blank and set the run interval to 30 minutes. Each run lists and reads files under the service's own identity, with the bucket policy authorizing every request. After one interval, confirm that the merged files exist under ingest/compacted/ and that their combined size matches the source files.

This guide explains how to grant the Marlin Notebooks job runner access to the bucket research-datasets, from which it reads input datasets and to which it writes job outputs. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named marlin-runner-role with a trust policy that names the service principal marlin-notebooks.svc as allowed to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:GetObject on arn:objstore:::research-datasets/inputs/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket for the inputs/ prefix. Allow storage:PutObject on arn:objstore:::research-datasets/job-output/* in the same policy, where each job writes results to a folder named after its job ID. In the runner's project settings, select marlin-runner-role as the job role. The runner assumes this role for every job and discards the credentials when the job ends. Run a sample notebook that reads one input file and verify that its results are stored under job-output/ in a folder named after the job ID.
